page.layout: One printed page (left page not shown, scan shows a single text page). One text block in the centre: Syriac, Samaritan, Persian and Arabic-Syriac polyglot passages with English-style Latin glosses, followed by the section heading XLI and a Greek passage ending with a catchword "Lati-". No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Syriaca : [illegible, ~30 letters] h.e. Et pone super thoracem Judicii luciduni & perfectum, eruntque super pectus ejus, quando ingredietur coram Domino : Et portabit Haroa Judicia filiorum Israël super pectus suum coram Domino semper.

Samaritana : [illegible, ~30 letters] : Hoc est : Facies quoque Urim & Tummim, ponesque super Rationale judicii [pectinatoris] Urim& Tummim, [Elucidationes &Perfectiones] ut sint super cor Aharonis,cùmingredietur coram Domino : feretque Aharon Judicium filiorum Israël super cor suum ante Dominum in perpetuum. Arabica literis Syris: [illegible, ~40 letters]

[illegible, ~40 letters] Hoc est : Et pones in thorace præparato Dilucidationes & Certitudines, & erunt super pectus Haron in ejus ingressu ad Habitaculum DEI : portabitque Haron repræsentationem filiorum Israël super cor suum ante habitaculum DEI semper. Persica: [illegible, ~40 letters] Hoc est : Dabis autem in humerali judicii Urim & Tummim & erunt supra cor Aharon in ingressu suo coram Domino: gestabitque Aharon judicium filiorum Israël supra cor suum coram Domino semper.
main_text.head: XLI. Sic fuerunt Versiones Orientales, ex Occidente dabimus Græcam, Latinam Vulgatam, Italicam, Gallicam & Anglicam.
main_text.p: Et Græca quidem [illegible, ~10 letters] LXX est talis: Καὶ ἐπιδήσεις ἐπὶ τὸ λογεῖον τῆς κρίσεως τὴν δήλωσιν καὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ἔσαι ἐπὶ τῆς καρδίας Ἀαρὼν, ὅταν εἰσπορεύηται εἰς τὸ ἅγιον ἐναντι κυρίου. Καὶ ὄψει Ἀαρὼν τὰς κρίσεις τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ τῆς καρδίας ἐναντι κυρίου διαπαντός.

page.notes: The Syriac, Samaritan, Arabic and Persian lines are largely illegible at this scan resolution and are marked accordingly. Verse sequence and the Greek passage are copied from the visible print; the Greek is uncertain in places.
